title: To-do List
blurb: Your own to-do list, saved in a file
intro: This time you'll build a to-do list program! Pick a number from the menu to write a task down, then view what you wrote. It saves to a file like in Chapter 11, so even the task you just added is read back from the file.
finale: You did it! Add a few tasks and check them with 2. In this app, todo.txt disappears when a round ends, but if you run it with Python on your own computer, it will still be there next time.

play.prompt: Type a menu number or a task

steps.goal: Show a menu and quit with 3
steps.task: Put the starter's print line inside while True: (one level, 4 spaces). Below it, read the chosen number with menu = input(). If menu is "3", print "Bye!" and end the loop with break. Any other number shows the menu again.

steps.explain: while True keeps showing the menu, and choosing 3 leaves with break. A menu program always needs a way out like this, or it never stops.

steps.goal: Read a task and write it to the file
steps.task: Below the if branch, add elif menu == "1":. Inside it, read a task with input() into item, open the file with with open("todo.txt", "a") as f:, and write one line with f.write(item + "\n"). Then print it with an f-string like "Added: laundry".

hints: "a" is the mode that adds to the end of the file (Chapter 11). Each time you write, the earlier tasks stay.
write() doesn't start a new line for you. Add "\n" after item so each task gets its own line.

steps.solution:
while True:
    print("1 Add · 2 View · 3 Quit")
    menu = input()
    if menu == "3":
        print("Bye!")
        break
    elif menu == "1":
        item = input()
        with open("todo.txt", "a") as f:
            f.write(item + "\n")
        print(f"Added: {item}")
steps.explain: Opening in "a" mode adds each task as a line at the end of the file. The file closes by itself when the with block ends. For now you only see the confirmation, but the next step reads this file back.

steps.goal: Read the file back and show it
steps.task: Add elif menu == "2":. Inside it, open the file with with open("todo.txt") as f:, take one line at a time with for line in f:, and print it with print("-", line.strip()) like "- laundry". The task you just added is read back from the file in the same run.

hints: Leave the mode out when reading. for line in f: hands you the file one line at a time (Chapter 11). Take the \n off each line with strip().
If earlier tasks vanish, check that the 1 branch opens with "a". If tasks run together like "- laundrygroceries", check that you add "\n" after item. The bug may be in your step 2 code.
steps.explain: You opened the same todo.txt for reading and showed it line by line. Since you added with "a", both the tasks you wrote and the ones already in the file are still there.

steps.goal: When there are no tasks yet
steps.task: Choosing 2 before writing anything gives a FileNotFoundError, because todo.txt doesn't exist yet. Put the View branch's with block inside try: (4 more spaces), and below it add except FileNotFoundError: that prints "No tasks yet".

hints: If something inside try: raises an error, Python jumps to except (Chapter 10). With no error, except is skipped.
Wrap only the with block in the View branch. If try wraps the whole while, the program ends right after the message.
steps.explain: except FileNotFoundError catches the missing-file error and turns it into a friendly message. The program doesn't stop, and the menu comes back.

steps.goal: Load the list when the program starts
steps.task: At the very top (above while), set n = 0. Inside try:, open todo.txt and add 1 to n with n += 1 for each line in for line in f:. On the line after the with block (still inside try), print an f-string like "Tasks loaded: 2" with n. If the file is missing, print "Starting a new list" in except FileNotFoundError:.

Put the count print inside try, below the with block. Outside try, "Tasks loaded: 0" would also show when there's no file.
steps.explain: Right at the start, the program reads the file and tells you how many tasks there are. Tasks you add from the menu pile up in the same file, so 2 can read them back any time. Now it's a real to-do list!
